sources.quote: The latest case-by-case Immigration Court records show that detained immigrants seeking release on bond have widely differing outcomes depending upon where they are being held.
sources.searcher_note: Pattern: immigration-judge bond grant rates vary by detention location (3% to 45%); names Washington, Florida, Colorado, Texas (Conroe), Arizona sites, not Louisiana or Pennsylvania; bond granted, not posted.

sources.outlet: The Lens (co-published by Louisiana Illuminator, Bolts)
sources.quote: DHS instituted a policy of mandatory detention, declaring that any immigrant who’d entered the U.S. “illegally” was ineligible for bond
sources.searcher_note: Louisiana detainees, including long-time residents, held without bond under the 2025 no-bond policy and Fifth Circuit law; no bond-posted rate, no comparison with Pennsylvania. Page says updated 2026-07-17.

sources.quote: The grant rate varies dramatically by court. Judges in some courts grant bond at 10-15x the rate of others
sources.searcher_note: National bond grant rate 4.3% (data through Feb 2026); court variation in general, no state breakdown.

notes: No source found giving ICE bond-posted rates by state, or for people arrested 2+ years after entry, or the Louisiana 7% / Texas 12% / Pennsylvania 29% split. Coverage found is about immigration-judge bond grant rates (a different measure from bond posted) and about the 2025 no-bond policy and the Fifth vs Third Circuit split. bklg.org blog (2026-05-12) fetched: Fifth Circuit decided the most bond requests, no state rates; not recorded. New Jersey Monitor 2026-07-14 piece on detainees increasingly denied bond returned 403, not recorded. Post-cutoff legal coverage exists of the circuit split (Third Circuit, covering Pennsylvania, ruled 2026-08-28 in Buele Morocho that long-time residents get bond hearings; Fifth Circuit, covering Louisiana and Texas, upheld no-bond detention), but those are rulings and explainers with no bond-posted numbers; not recorded.
